why: a macOS or Linux home path. The segment after /Users/ or /home/ IS the account name, so the path identifies its owner and does not exist on anyone else's machine. AUTO-RESOLVABLE: $HOME is the correct portable form, so this one substitution is mechanical and unambiguous — it is a refuse-tier rule that carries a 'to', which is why it fixes rather than blocks

the Windows form of the same leak (C:\Users\<account>). NO 'to' ON PURPOSE, unlike path-home-unix: there is no single portable spelling that is right in both a shell line and a prose sentence, and guessing one would quietly rewrite a path into something that does not work. Reported and blocked, so a human picks the replacement. Git Bash is this project's documented Windows floor, which is why the form is covered at all
the Google Drive mount form on macOS; the segment that follows it is the account address the Drive belongs to
a Drive mount embeds a full email address in the path itself — the account name is part of the directory name, so the path leaks the address even when no address is written out
OpenAI-style API key
Anthropic API key — the hyphen after 'ant' means key-openai cannot catch this form
GitHub personal-access / OAuth / server / refresh token
GitHub fine-grained personal access token
Google API key
Google OAuth access token — the Google auth path issues these
Slack bot/app/user token
AWS access key id
an embedded private key of any type
a bearer token pasted into a doc, script or example

a credential assigned to a named variable — catches key formats no shape-rule anticipates. PATTERN FIXED 2026-08-05 (ReDoS, red-team-found): the old form had two adjacent star-quantified groups sharing the space character (`["' ]*` then `\s*`) — ambiguous over any run of spaces, O(n^2) backtracking on a failed match (a 60KB padded file took ~14-22s). Merged into a single `["'\s]*` quantifier over the union charset before the `[:=]` — same matches, no ambiguity

a Google Sheet/Doc/Slides/Form/Drive-file/folder ID embedded in a URL. The ID names ONE specific resource in ONE specific account — it is an address, not a shape, and it does not exist on anyone else's install. Ported 2026-08-15 from the donor lane, where a live tree sweep found real Sheet, Tasks-list and Calendar IDs that no prior rule caught. Anchored to the URL prefix on purpose: a bare 15-char token is not distinctive enough to block on

a Google resource ID (Sheet/Doc/Folder/Calendar/Tasks-list) assigned to a named variable or config key — catches the same identifier when it never appears inside a URL, which is the form a config file uses. Mirrors key-assignment's proven shape, including its single merged `["'\s]*` quantifier so it carries no ReDoS ambiguity either. The closing quote is REQUIRED, so a documented placeholder (`sheet_id: <paste yours>`) does not match. Ported 2026-08-15 from the donor lane

the domain suffix of a SECONDARY Google Calendar's private address. This string only ever appears attached to one specific long private hash, so its presence identifies that a particular calendar is being named even when the hash itself has been truncated or removed — which is exactly the residue a hash-only scrub leaves behind. Deliberately does NOT require the hash, for that reason. Ported 2026-08-15 from the donor lane. HONEST BOUND: documentation that shows the address FORM with a placeholder hash still matches, and that is intended — a human clears it in seconds, and the alternative is trusting that every future writer remembers to elide the suffix too

an ntfy.sh push-notification topic in URL form. A topic is an UNAUTHENTICATED inbox address: anyone holding the string can read every message sent to it and publish to it, so it is closer to a credential than to a name. The trailing path segment is required, so naming the service itself in prose does not match. Ported 2026-08-15 from the donor lane

a private-range (RFC 1918) IP address — typically a home router or a LAN device. Unroutable from the internet, but it still discloses the shape of the operator's home network, which is why it is an address leak and not a harmless constant. Ported 2026-08-15 from the donor lane, which added it after a live sweep found a real router address no prior rule caught. TIER DELIBERATELY CHANGED ON PORT: the donor filed this as '2-private'. In THIS repo '2-private' means 'compiled from the reader's own identity file' — identity_rules.py stamps it, judge.py labels it 'the terms this person listed as identifying them', and verify_rules.py uses the mere PRESENCE of a 2-private rule as its proof that the personal tier is not empty. A SHIPPED 2-private rule would satisfy that proof forever and silently retire the one check that catches a reader whose identity tier never compiled. Filed '1-identity' — the tier judge.py already calls 'path and account shapes' — so the check keeps its teeth. HONEST BOUND: a private IP is also a common GENERIC example in networking documentation and will occasionally be a false positive on one — accepted, because missing a real router address is worse than a block a human clears in seconds
